meta.titre: ICT Output Devices: how printers and displays work and how to compare them

sections.contenu_markdown: In a cyber cafe in Douala, one customer prints a school report on a laser printer while a shopkeeper next door prints a three-part invoice on an old noisy printer that strikes the paper. Both are output devices, but they work in very different ways and suit different jobs. The GCE ICT papers regularly ask candidates to explain how a printer works, to compare printers and to say how their speed and quality are measured. Clear, ordered answers with the right vocabulary earn full marks.

items: Output is the result that a computer presents to the user after processing.
A picture on a screen is made of very small dots called pixels.
One minute equals 60 seconds, and one hour equals 60 minutes.

sections.titre: Output devices: displays and printers, how they work and how to compare them
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Output devices
An **output device** turns processed data into a form that people can use. **Softcopy** output is temporary and shown on a screen or through speakers; **hardcopy** output is permanent and printed on paper (or other material). Monitors, projectors and speakers give softcopy; printers and plotters give hardcopy.

### Displays
A monitor shows a picture made of **pixels**. The **resolution** is the number of pixels across by the number down: 1920 × 1080 means 1920 × 1080 = 2,073,600 pixels. A higher resolution gives a sharper picture. A projector enlarges the picture for a group.

### Printers
| Printer | Principle | Strengths | Weaknesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dot matrix (impact) | Pins in the print head strike an inked ribbon against the paper, forming characters from dots | Cheap to run; prints several copies at once on carbon or multipart forms | Noisy, slow, low quality, poor graphics |
| Inkjet (non-impact) | Nozzles spray tiny drops of liquid ink on the paper | Good colour and photo quality; low purchase price | Ink is dear per page; slower; wet pages may smudge |
| Laser (non-impact) | A laser draws the page as a pattern of electric charge on a drum; toner powder sticks to the pattern, is transferred to the paper and melted on by heat | Fast, sharp, quiet, cheap per page for large jobs | High purchase price |
| Thermal (non-impact) | Heat darkens special heat-sensitive paper | Small, silent; receipts and tickets | Prints fade; special paper |

An **impact** printer touches the paper through a ribbon; a **non-impact** printer does not.

### Quality and speed
Print **quality** depends on the **resolution**, measured in **dots per inch (dpi)**, on the number of colours it can print and on the quality of the ink or toner and paper. Print **speed** is measured in **pages per minute (ppm)** for page printers and in **characters per second (cps)** for dot matrix printers. Speed figures usually refer to plain text; photographs and full-colour pages print more slowly.

### Connection
A printer is joined to the computer by a USB or network cable or wirelessly, and needs its **driver**. Once it is connected and switched on, its power or status light shows and the computer normally lists it as ready (online) with no error message.

variantes.nom: Explaining how a laser printer works
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the mode of functioning of a laser printer.
variantes.contenu_markdown: 1. The page is received and converted into a pattern of dots in the printer's memory. 2. A drum is given an even electric charge. 3. A laser beam, swept across the drum by a rotating mirror, forms the image as a pattern of charge. 4. Toner powder sticks to the charged pattern. 5. The paper passes the drum and takes up the toner. 6. Heated rollers (the fuser) melt the toner so that it bonds to the paper. Write the steps in this order.

variantes.nom: Explaining how a dot matrix printer works
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the mode of functioning of a dot matrix or other impact printer.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The print head moves across the paper. It carries a column of tiny pins (commonly 9 or 24). For each character, the controller fires the chosen pins, which strike the inked ribbon and leave dots on the paper; the pattern of dots forms the character. The paper then moves up one line. Because the pins strike, several copies can be made at once, but the printing is noisy and the quality is low.

variantes.nom: Choosing a printer and comparing costs
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a scenario gives needs (receipts, copies, colour photos, large volumes) or running costs.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Receipts and tickets: thermal. Multipart carbon forms: dot matrix. Occasional colour photographs: inkjet. Many pages every day: laser. Running cost per page = price of a cartridge ÷ number of pages it prints. Total cost = purchase price + number of pages × cost per page.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A print shop in Douala must print a report of 90 pages of plain text. Its laser printer prints 18 pages per minute. An old dot matrix printer prints at 200 characters per second, and each page holds 3,000 characters.

(a) Calculate the time needed on the laser printer.

(b) Calculate the time on the dot matrix printer, in minutes.

(c) How many times longer is the dot matrix printer?

(d) Give one reason why the shop might still keep the dot matrix printer.

etapes.action: Identify the unit of speed of each printer.
etapes.justification: The laser speed is in pages per minute and the dot matrix speed is in characters per second, so the figures cannot be compared before conversion.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Convert both to a time for the whole report.

etapes.justification: Time = number of pages ÷ pages per minute.

etapes.action: Find the time for one page on the dot matrix printer.
etapes.justification: Time per page = characters per page ÷ characters per second.

etapes.action: Find the time for the whole report and convert to minutes.
etapes.justification: Multiply by the number of pages, then divide by 60 to obtain minutes.
The ratio shows the difference in speed; the reason for keeping an impact printer is a feature that a laser printer lacks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 22.5 ÷ 5 = **4.5 times** longer. The dot matrix printer can print carbon copies of forms in one pass, which a laser printer cannot do.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The laser printer needs 5 minutes and the dot matrix printer 22.5 minutes, which is 4.5 times longer. The shop keeps the dot matrix printer for multipart forms.

items.erreur_markdown: "A laser printer is an impact printer because the laser hits the paper."
items.pourquoi_faux: The laser beam does not touch the paper. It forms a pattern of charge on a drum, and toner is transferred to the paper, so the printer is non-impact.
items.correction_markdown: "A laser printer is a non-impact printer." Dot matrix is the example of an impact printer.

items.erreur_markdown: "A dot matrix printer sprays ink onto the paper."
items.pourquoi_faux: Spraying drops of ink describes an inkjet printer. A dot matrix printer strikes an inked ribbon with pins.
items.correction_markdown: "Pins strike an inked ribbon against the paper and form characters from dots."

items.erreur_markdown: "The speed of a printer is measured in dpi."
items.pourquoi_faux: Dots per inch measures the resolution, which affects quality. Speed is measured in pages per minute or characters per second.
items.correction_markdown: "Speed is measured in ppm (page printers) or cps (dot matrix); quality is measured by dpi."

items.erreur_markdown: "Resolution is the size of the screen in inches."
items.pourquoi_faux: Screen size is the length of the diagonal. Resolution is the number of pixels across and down, or the dots per inch for a printer.
items.correction_markdown: "Resolution is the number of pixels horizontally by vertically (for example 1920 × 1080)."

items.erreur_markdown: "A monitor gives hardcopy because the text can be read."
items.pourquoi_faux: Hardcopy is permanent output on paper. The picture on a monitor disappears when the screen is switched off or changed.
items.correction_markdown: "A monitor gives softcopy; a printer gives hardcopy."

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Classify each device as hardcopy or softcopy output: a printer, a monitor, a pair of speakers, a plotter, a projector.

(b) For each of these printers, say whether it is an impact or a non-impact printer: dot matrix, laser, inkjet.

(c) State the unit of speed of a laser printer and the unit of speed of a dot matrix printer.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Hardcopy: **printer, plotter**. Softcopy: **monitor, speakers, projector**.

(b) Dot matrix: **impact**. Laser: **non-impact**. Inkjet: **non-impact**.

(c) Laser: **pages per minute (ppm)**. Dot matrix: **characters per second (cps)**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A monitor has a resolution of 1280 × 1024 pixels. A newer one has 1920 × 1080 pixels.

(a) Calculate the number of pixels on each monitor.

(b) By how many pixels do they differ, and how many times more pixels does the newer one have (two decimal places)?

(c) A photograph measuring 4 inches by 6 inches is printed at 300 dots per inch. How many dots across and down, and how many in total?

An office compares two printers. Laser: price 120,000 FCFA, a toner cartridge costs 48,000 FCFA and prints 2,400 pages, speed 20 pages per minute. Inkjet: price 45,000 FCFA, a cartridge costs 12,000 FCFA and prints 300 pages, speed 8 pages per minute.

(a) Calculate the running cost per page of each printer.

(b) Calculate the total cost of buying each printer and printing 6,000 pages.

(c) After how many pages do the two total costs become equal?

(d) Calculate the time to print 6,000 pages on each printer, in hours.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Laser: 48,000 ÷ 2,400 = **20 FCFA** per page. Inkjet: 12,000 ÷ 300 = **40 FCFA** per page.

(b) Laser: 120,000 + 6,000 × 20 = **240,000 FCFA**. Inkjet: 45,000 + 6,000 × 40 = **285,000 FCFA**.

(c) Let n be the number of pages: 120,000 + 20n = 45,000 + 40n, so 20n = 75,000 and n = **3,750 pages**. (Check: both cost 195,000 FCFA.) Beyond this number the laser printer is cheaper.

(d) Laser: 6,000 ÷ 20 = 300 minutes = **5 hours**. Inkjet: 6,000 ÷ 8 = 750 minutes = **12.5 hours**.

items_markdown: Softcopy output (screen, speakers, projector) is temporary; hardcopy output (printer, plotter) is permanent.
Resolution is the number of pixels across by the number down for a screen, and dots per inch (dpi) for a printer; a higher resolution gives a sharper result.
Dot matrix printers are impact printers (pins strike an inked ribbon); laser, inkjet and thermal printers are non-impact.
Laser printing steps: charge the drum, draw the image with the laser, attach toner, transfer it to the paper, fuse it with heat.
Print quality depends on dpi, colours and ink or toner quality; speed is measured in ppm or cps, never in dpi.
Running cost per page = cartridge price ÷ pages per cartridge; compare total cost = purchase price + pages × cost per page.
